title: Go: File I/O
description: Read, write, and manipulate files using Go's os and bufio packages.

steps.title: Read entire file
steps.description: Use `os.ReadFile` to read "input.txt" and print its contents as a string using `fmt.Printf("Content: %s\n", data)`. Handle any error by printing "Error: ...".
hints: Check the error — file may not exist

verification.failureMessage: Make sure to convert the byte slice to a string for printing.

steps.title: Write entire file
steps.description: Use `os.WriteFile` to write "Hello, File!" to "output.txt". Print "Wrote to output.txt" on success or handle the error.
hints: Third argument is the file permission bits (644 = rw-r--r--)
If the file exists, it will be overwritten

verification.failureMessage: Convert the string to []byte before passing to WriteFile.

steps.title: Open and scan line by line
steps.description: Use `os.Open` and `bufio.NewScanner` to read "input.txt" line by line. Print each line prefixed with its line number: "Line 1: <content>".
hints: `os.Open` returns a file handle, `bufio.NewScanner(f)` wraps it
Use `scanner.Scan()` in a for loop and `scanner.Text()` for the line
Close the file with `defer f.Close()` after opening

verification.successMessage: File scanned line by line with bufio.Scanner!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure your loop iterates while scanner.Scan() returns true.

steps.title: Create and write with buffered writer
steps.description: Use `os.Create` and `bufio.NewWriter` to write lines to "lines.txt". Write 3 lines: "Line A", "Line B", "Line C" (each with a newline). Print "Wrote 3 lines to lines.txt".
hints: Call `writer.Flush()` after writing all lines to flush to disk

verification.failureMessage: You must call Flush() or the data may not be written.

steps.title: File existence check
steps.description: Check if a file "test.txt" exists using `os.Stat`. Print "File exists" if it does, or print the error ("File does not exist") if os.IsNotExist returns true for the error.
hints: Use `os.IsNotExist(err)` to check if the error is "file not found"
If err is nil, the file exists and info is returned

verification.successMessage: File existence check with os.Stat completed!
verification.failureMessage: Use os.Stat and os.IsNotExist to check for the file.
